task_instance: User asks: 'How do I flash JetPack onto my Jetson Orin Nano devkit?' — perform the skill's discovery workflow: query the live NVIDIA skills catalog and recommend the best-matching skill(s) with install command and first prompt, without installing anything.
evidence: Ran `npx skills add nvidia/skills --list` from the work directory (cd'd in first). It cloned https://github.com/nvidia/skills.git live and discovered 382 skills, output saved to npx_full_raw.txt / npx_full_clean.txt (ANSI-stripped, 1544 lines). Searched the cleaned catalog output for jetson/jetpack/bsp terms (grep -n -i 'jetson|jetpack|l4t|bsp|sdk.manager' npx_full_clean.txt) and found a strong, current catalog match: jetson-flash-image ('Use to flash a promoted BSP image to a Jetson DUT in RCM mode via flash.sh or l4t_initrd_flash.sh.'), plus supporting skills jetson-download-bsp and jetson-quick-start. Followed the skill's Recommendation Format and Confidence Rules to produce the actual deliverable: a ranked (<=3) recommendation list with skill name, why it fits, install command, and first useful prompt for each, written to recommendation_output.txt. Per the skill's own rule ('Ask before installing. Do not run npx skills add unless the user approves.'), no `--skill <name>` install was executed since no user approval was possible in this single-turn simulation — this is correct behavior per the skill's spec, not a blocker. Verified deliverable by inspecting recommendation_output.txt content and confirming the matched skill names/descriptions exactly mirror strings present in the live catalog output (grep matches at lines 650-653 of npx_full_clean.txt for jetson-flash-image). Files produced: npx_list_output.txt, npx_full_raw.txt, npx_full_clean.txt, clean_list.txt, recommendation_output.txt, result.json — all under the work directory.
